question: Which of the following Statutory Commissions was set up to study the working of the government after the Government of India Act 1919 was passed?
solution:
The correct answer is __**The Simon Commission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Simon Commission was constituted in **1927** to review the working of the constitutional system in India as per the Government of India Act 1919.
 
• It was a seven-member commission chaired by **Sir John Simon**.
 
• The commission was boycotted by Indian political parties because it did not include any Indian members.
 
• The report of the Simon Commission led to the Government of India Act 1935, which introduced provincial autonomy and the establishment of federal courts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Government of India Act 1919**

 
 
• Also known as the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms.
 
• Introduced a dual system of governance (dyarchy) in the provinces.
 
• Separate electorates were expanded and more power was given to the provincial legislative councils.
 
 
 
• **Government of India Act 1935**
 
 
• This act provided for the establishment of an All-India Federation.
 
• It introduced provincial autonomy, allowing elected Indian representatives to form governments.
 
• It also established a federal court and expanded the franchise.
 
 
 
• **Butler Commission**
 
 
• Set up in 1927 to examine the relationship between the princely states and the British Crown.
 
• Recommended that the relationship should be direct and not through the Government of India.
 
 
 
• **Hunter Commission**
 
 
• Formed in 1919 to investigate the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
 
• Condemned the actions of General Dyer, who ordered the massacre, but did not impose any severe penalties.
